questions.question_text: The onset of very early onset schizophrenia is before the age of
questions.explanation:
In very early onset schizophrenia, the onset of psychotic symptoms is at or before the age of 13. Early onset schizophrenia is a term used to
indicate the onset of psychotic symptoms before the age of 18.

questions.question_text: Tom, aged 12, has been diagnosed with NREM sleep disorder. The most likely diagnosis is;
questions.explanation:
NREM Sleep disorders include Sleep walking, sleep terrors and confusion arousals. REM sleep parasomnias include REM behavioural
disorder, Night mares and Sleep paralysis.

questions.question_text: Which of the following drug should be avoided in an ADHD child with liver dysfunction?
questions.explanation:
Atomoxetine should be avoided in children with preexisting liver disease. Parents should be warned of the possibilities of liver diesase
emerging and advised of the possible features they might notice.LFTs monitoring is needed.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is a feature of dual role transvestism?

options.text: Male wearing clothes of the other sex without desire for permanent change and no sexual arousal
Male with persistent discomfort with his sex
Male wearing clothes of the other sex to achieve sexual pleasure and associated with masturbation
Male using shoes to obtain sexual pleasure
Male with a persistent preoccupation with castration

correct_answer.text: Male wearing clothes of the other sex without desire for permanent change and no sexual arousal

questions.explanation:
Various degrees of gender dysphoria exist. One mild form is recognized in ICD and DSM as dual role transvestism. The individual wears
clothes of the opposite sex in order to experience temporary membership in the opposite sex. The individual experiences a sense of
appropriateness by wearing clothes of the other gender.There is no sexual motivation for the cross-dressing. The individual has no desire
for a permanent change to the opposite sex.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is most predictive of nocturnal enuresis in children?
questions.explanation:
Association of enuresis has been made with a high rate of stressful life events, UTI, constipation , and with children of low socioeconomic
background, living in large families or overcrowded conditions.

questions.question_text: Which of the following psychotic disorders with onset in childhood has the worst prognosis?
questions.explanation:
There is limited data on recovery rates from childhood onset schizophrenia but given that the emergence of the disorder disrupts
psychosocial development and schooling. It is unsurprising the very early onset schizophrenia and early onset schizophrenia often has a
relatively poor prognosis even with psychopharmacological treatment. 80-90% will have 2 or more episodes in a 5-year period. Presence of
a�ective symptoms o�ers a better outcome.

questions.question_text:
A teenager attends the CAMHS clinic for sleep problems and noted to have poor sleep hygiene. Which of the following advice should be
given as a sleep hygiene measure?

options.text: Avoid large meals prior to bed
Having a cold bath 1-2 hours before bedtime
Try to do strenuous exercise in the 4 hours before bedtime
Try to sleep even when you are not actually feeling tired or sleepy
If you have a bad night sleep, change your daytime routine

correct_answer.text: Avoid large meals prior to bed

questions.explanation:
"A healthy, balanced diet will help you to sleep well, but timing is important. Some people �nd that a very empty stomach at bedtime is
distracting, so it can be useful to have a light snack, but a heavy meal soon before bed can also interrupt sleep. Only try to sleep when you
actually feel tired or sleepy, rather than spending too much time awake in bed. Even if you have a bad night sleep and are tired it is
important that you try to keep your daytime activities the same as you had planned. That is, don't avoid activities because you feel tired. This
can reinforce the insomnia. Having a hot bath 1-2 hours before bedtime can be useful, as it will raise your body temperature, causing you to
feel sleepy as your body temperature drops again". (Excerpt from: www.cci.health.wa.gov.au Also see: Tan E, et al. BMC pediatrics. 2012 Dec
7;12(1):1.)

questions.question_text:
A young boy is referred to your CAMHS clinic. He has signi�cant communication di�culties and more recently has been su�ering from
seizures. What is the most common feature of seizures in autism?
questions.explanation:
Roughly a third of individuals with autism will develop seizures. In the majority, seizures will begin after the age of 10, generalized tonic-
clonic seizures predominate and prevalence is greater in females. (Bolton et al, 2011)

questions.question_text: What speci�c dietary advice would you give to a mother whose child has been diagnosed with ADHD?

options.text: Stress the need for a balanced diet

correct_answer.text: Stress the need for a balanced diet

questions.explanation:
Studies on ADHD children showed that a well-balanced diet, including vegetables, complex carbohydrates, fruits, and plenty of protein,
helped to bring hyperactive behaviour under control consistently.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is an advanced sign of opioid withdrawal
questions.explanation:
The opioid withdrawal symptoms are given below; the early signs of withdrawal include anxiety & craving for opioids, fear of withdrawal.
Agitation, insomnia, headache, lacrimation, rhinorrhoea, yawning, shivering and perspiration follow this. Dilated pupils and piloerection are
late signs followed by tachycardia, increase in respiratory rate and abdominal cramps. The Advanced sign of opioid withdrawal is Muscle
spasm.

questions.question_text: Which of the following is true about Korsako�'s psychosis?

options.text: Thiamine is the treatment of choice
About 10 % alcoholic patients recovering from Wernicke's encephalopathy develop Korsako�'s syndrome.
Marked de�cits noted in attention, procedural and working memory

correct_answer.text: Thiamine is the treatment of choice

questions.explanation:
About 80 per cent of alcoholic patients recovering from Wernicke's encephalopathy develop Korsako�'s amnesic syndrome. It is
characterized by marked de�cits in anterograde and to some extent retrograde episodic memory, apathy, an intact sensorium, and relative
preservation of other intellectual abilities such as attention, procedural memory and working memory. Diagnosis of Korsako�s syndrome
correlates best with the presence of lesions in the dorsomedial thalamus. But lesions in the mammillary bodies, the mammillo-thalamic
tractand the anterior thalamus may be more important to memory dysfunctionthan lesions in the medial dorsal nucleus of the thalamus.
Confabulation occurs due to a double lesion – frontal de�cits and diencephalic de�cits. In terms of treatment, continue oral thiamine
replacement for up to 2 years.

questions.question_text:

questions.explanation:
Child and adolescent behaviour modi�cation can occur at the national, school and individual level, depending on the type of intervention.
School-based interventions would best; be focused on speci�c age groups (as the issue surrounding drinking will not apply to children of all
ages), be more general (as any pupil with alcohol dependence will require an individual approach), explore existing attitudes of children
towards drinking and be facilitated by a nominated member of sta� or visiting expert speaker.

questions.question_text: Which one among the following test is a speci�c biomarker for heavy alcohol misuse?
questions.explanation:
Carbohydrate De�cient Transferrin (CDT) is a biomarker for heavy alcohol consumption. The Carbohydrate De�cient Transferrin (CDT) test is
a particularly speci�c in tracking heavy alcohol consumption over an extended period of time. The advantage of using CDT in testing for
alcohol misuse is it is una�ected by mild alcohol related liver disease or fatty liver (due to obesity, diabetes etc) which can falsely increase γ -
glutamyl transferase (GGT), the enzyme in blood most commonly used to indicate excess alcohol consumption. CDT is also una�ected by
chronic disease or B12/folate de�ciencies which can increase the mean corpuscular volume (MCV), another blood test used to detect alcohol
misuse. Transferrin remains in the circulation for 7 to 14 days and CDT, therefore, can give an indication of alcohol consumption over this
period of time, which gives it an advantage over blood or urine alcohol measurements, which only remain elevated for 24-48 hours after
alcohol consumption. (Bergström, J.P. and Helander, A., 2008. Alcohol and alcoholism, 43(4), pp.436-441.)

questions.question_text:
A 23-year-old female student with anorexia nervosa has recently been admitted to your Eating Disorders unit. Which of the following would
lead you to immediately referring this patient to a medical hospital?

options.text: Her heart rate is 58 beats per minute

questions.explanation:
In patients with anorexia nervosa, hospital admission should only be considered in the presence of serious medical or psychiatric problems.
This patient's blood test revealed a severe hypokalemia placing her at a greater risk of cardiac complications such as arrhythmias, which is
the most common cause of death in patients with anorexia nervosa (mortality rate ~ 10%) (Ref: Oxford Handbook of Psychiatry).

questions.question_text:
You are reviewing a 52-year-old lady with paranoid schizophrenia who requires medical treatment for her symptoms. She has a history of
breast cancer. Which of the following would be the LEAST appropriate medication to prescribe her?
questions.explanation:
Treatment with amisulpride can induce hyperprolactinaemia, a long-term consequence of which is a possible increase in the risk of breast
cancer. The antipsychotics that are not usually associated with hyperprolactinaemia include Aripiprazole, Olanzapine, Quetiapine and
Clozapine (for more details see SPMM Smart Revise Notes)

questions.question_text: Anorexia nervosa in adulthood is most commonly associated with which of the following?
questions.explanation: Anorexia nervosa is most commonly associated with obsessive and other anxious personality traits.

tardive dyskinesia. Which antipsychotic would be suitable to be used in this situation?
questions.explanation:
The use of Clozapine is probably best supported in this regard, but Quetiapine, another weak striatal dopamine antagonist is also e�ective.
(Ref: The Maudlsey prescribing guidelines-11th edition; 107)

questions.question_text: Which one among the following is a signi�cant risk factor for the development of Neuroleptic malignant syndrome?
questions.explanation:
Risk factors for NMS: High ambient temperature, dehydration, patient agitation or catatonia, rapid antipsychotic initiation/dose escalation,
withdrawal of anti-parkinsonian medication, use of high potency agents/depot IM preparations, history of organic brain disease such as
dementia, history of a�ective disorder, previous history of NMS, Predisposing drugs like lithium and anticholinergic medications. (Ref:
Oxford Handbook of Psychiatry-882)

questions.question_text: Severe lithium toxicity presents with which of the following signs?
questions.explanation:
Central Nervous System features of severe lithium toxicity: Blackout spells, epileptiform seizures, slurred speech, dizziness, vertigo,
incontinence of urine or feces, somnolence, psychomotor retardation, restlessness, confusion, stupor, coma, acute dystonia, downbeat
nystagmus. (Ref: McKnight RF, et al. Lithium toxicity pro�le: a systematic review and meta-analysis. The Lancet. 2012 Mar 2;379(9817):721-8.)

against depression?
questions.explanation: Lamotrigine has good evidence in prophylaxis in bipolar a�ective disorder, especially when depressive episodes predominate.

baby and has �ashbacks. She �nds these thoughts anxiety provoking. She regards the birth as traumatic. What is her diagnosis?
questions.explanation:
Intrusive thoughts that cause anxiety are a feature of OCD, and there is a greater predisposition to this distressing experience following a
traumatic birth.

questions.question_text: What side e�ect would you monitor closely in a patient taking Donepezil?
questions.explanation:
Acetyl cholinesterase inhibitors (AChEs) like Donepezil may have vagotonic e�ects on heart rate leading to bradycardia. AChE inhibitors can
induce sinus bradycardia, sino-atrial block, and aggravate pre-existing sinus node disease and atrioventricular block (Savie et al, 1998).
Donepezil overdose has been reported to result in profound sinus bradycardia that can be reversed with atropine (Shepherd et al, 1999;
Hidetaka et al, 2003). Therefore it is important to monitor for signs like bradycardia.

questions.question_text: What type of memory is most a�ected by ECT?
questions.explanation:
Retrograde memory i.e. the recall of events that occurred before the treatment, is the most commonly a�ected aspect of memory following
Electro-Convulsive Therapy (ECT). It is an early side e�ect, occurs in 64% of patients receiving ECT and usually resolves completely.

questions.question_text: Which of the following strategies has good evidence in prescribing in treatment resistant depression?
questions.explanation:
"California rocket fuel" is a medical slang term for the combined administration of mirtazapine (a NaSSA) and venlafaxine (an SNRI). This
combination is usually used in the treatment of treatment-resistant depression. It is usually well tolerated, has excellent literature support
available and is widely used. However the patient should be informed of the theoretical risk of serotonin syndrome.

questions.question_text: 'Sequential Diagrammatic reformulation' (SDR) is seen in what type of therapy?
questions.explanation:
Sequential Diagrammatic Reformulation (SDR) is a technique used in Cognitive analytical therapy. It involves collaboratively developed visual
map of problematic patterns and reciprocal roles. The procedures are depicted and interlinked in �ow-chart format. The aim of such
diagrams is to amplify understanding of often-complex procedural sequences and their inter-relationships in a way that words alone cannot.
SDR's are often elaborated by around the sixth or seventh session. (Ref: Denman, C., 2001. Cognitive–analytic therapy. Advances in
Psychiatric treatment, 7(4), pp.243-252.)

questions.question_text:
Katie's mother had just died. However, she appears elated and happy to be keeping busy with funeral arrangements. The type of defense
mechanism used in this situation is called
questions.explanation:
Ego defences exist in order to protect us from aspects of reality that might overwhelm us if we made too much contact with them. The
defence mechanism employed in this situation is called Manic defence. The potential sadness and anguish about the mother's death is
defended against by 'acting out the opposite': a sense of elation.

progress. This phenomenon is called
questions.explanation:
Negative therapeutic reaction is a paradoxical phenomenon whereby a worsening of the patient's condition follows an acknowledgement of
progress. Freud thought it was linked to unconscious guilt about the progress during psychotherapy.

questions.question_text:
The prevalence of a condition is 10%. A new diagnostic test ('test A') has a sensitivity of 95% and false positive rate of 5%. What is the post
test probability?
questions.explanation:
According to Bayes' Theorem, if you know the pretest probability and likelihood ratio of a test, you can �nd the post test probability. There
are two ways of computing post-test probability. If you have Bayesian nomogram, you can simply connect the dots indicating pretest
probability and LR value, to get the third point indicating post-test probability. If you don't have a nomogram at hand, you have to then use
the following formula: post-test odds = pretest odds x LR (Note that this formula uses odds, not probability rates). In this question,
prevalence = pretest probability = 10/100. So pre test odds = 10/90 (as odds = probability / [1-probability]) LR+ = true positivity rate/ false
positivity rate ( i.e. sensitivity/[1-speci�city]) = 95%/5% = 19 So, post-test odds = pretest odds x LR = (10/90) x 19 = 190/90 = 19/9. If you know
the odds of an event, you can easily compute the probability. Use the formula probability = odds/[1+odds]. So post test probability =
(19/9)/[1+(19/9)] = 19/28 = 67.8% nearly 68%

questions.question_text: Which of the following constitutes primary prevention of pre-natal depression?
questions.explanation:

implemented before any evidence of disease. Pre-conception counseling is a form of pre-conceptual care that allows women and their

pregnancy, and be as healthy as possible. Based on their past psychiatric history, it identi�es couples at increased risk of psychiatric
complications during pregnancy and optimizes management of chronic mental illness. (Ref: Johnson, K., et al., 2006. Morbidity and Mortality
Weekly Report, 55(4), pp.1-23.)
